built.shiftWhy: the same crew held back four hours, paid at overtime. Twelve hours on the floor produces about 1.35 days of work, not 1.5 — the last hours are the tired ones. The commonest answer on a fit-out that is three weeks behind
built.why: every condition of handover lands by 2026-10-21 on general shift with overtime (09:00 to 22:00) with 10 gangs per trade, peaking at 127 people against a floor ceiling of 191. Labour cost runs about 1.6x. De-snagging and the handover file run on past the date, as they always do.

siteWorkBy.why: the client's snag walk, de-snagging to sign-off and the deep clean are 19 working days that no crew size compresses. Working back from 2026-10-21, every trade has to be off the floor by 2026-09-29

floor.why: one worker per 225 sqft is what a floor works at day after day with material movement, debris removal and one goods lift; one per 100 sqft is what it absorbs for a few weeks of finishing, when the trades are light and spread across every room

shifts.name: General shift
shifts.why: one crew, eight working hours and an hour off. The default, and what every norm in this engine is written against

shifts.name: General shift with overtime
shifts.why: the same crew held back four hours, paid at overtime. Twelve hours on the floor produces about 1.35 days of work, not 1.5 — the last hours are the tired ones. The commonest answer on a fit-out that is three weeks behind

shifts.name: Two shifts
shifts.why: two crews, day and night. The night crew produces about 85% of the day crew: the same hands, less supervision, no consultant to answer a question and a shared goods lift. Needs building permission for night work and a second set of supervisors

shifts.name: Round the clock
shifts.why: three crews of eight hours. Rarely worth it on an interior fit-out: the handover between shifts costs an hour each end, material cannot be moved into a tower at 3am, and the third crew is the hardest to staff. Here as the last thing before the date moves

verdict.why: the work fits the window at the floor's capacity

assumptions.what: the floor can hold one worker per 225 sqft, so 85 people at once
assumptions.why: 19,181 sqft measured off the drawing, at the congestion rate the levelling already uses
assumptions.affects: whether the date is reachable at all — it is the denominator of the whole answer
assumptions.settledBy: the site manager saying what this floor has actually held on a busy day
assumptions.instead: solving for crew size alone, which said 2.85x and put 1,188 people on a floor that holds 85

assumptions.what: the man-hour norms are right for this specification
assumptions.why: they are practitioner and Methvin figures held in platform/kb/durations.js, per man-hour and per unit, and they scale — but they are generic. Painting alone is 7% of the job at 0.71 mh/m2.
assumptions.affects: the total work content, and therefore the date
assumptions.settledBy: the package manager for painting confirming the output rate for what is actually specified
assumptions.instead: treating a generic norm as a measured fact

assumptions.why: 2 assumptions carrying this plan: 0 high, 2 medium, 0 low.
